transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-30 14:00 - 14:56 PDT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Stellar Procurement), Ethan Wu (Stellar Legal), Priya Nair (Stellar ML), Liam O'Connor (Stellar FinOps)

00:00 Jordan: ok good afternoon everyone, thanks for making the time. quick agenda — pricing clarity, msa/dpa exceptions, sla tolerances, and pilot gating.
00:23 Maya: hi thanks, yes we kicked this off from procurement. timeline is tight, leadership wants a vendor decision by mid-September so we'd like to confirm pathing.
00:31 Jordan: understood. Sofia will cover the tech bits and benchmark plan, i'll cover commercial.
00:38 Sofia: hey all, quick note on infra — Redwood Dedicate, Redwood Privet, whatever the right target is — we support hosted api, dedicated GPU pools and private v p c deployments. apologies — sometimes the transcript says redwood privet.
00:54 Priya: haha no worries. for us the big things are: data residency, kv cache behaviour with long convo histories, and how the k v cache is flushed for privacy reasons. also throughput: we expect bursts up to 600 qps for reranking endpoints.
01:12 Sofia: okay that helps. for 600 qps we'll likely recommend dedicated pool with auto-burst, and also prefix caching to cut token cost. i'll run the sample payloads you sent through our continuous batching bench to get latency/p99 and t p s.
01:28 Liam: on pricing side — we need a clear monthly commit band to present to finance. egress is a concern; do you bill network egress separate from tokens?
01:39 Jordan: yes we split token usage vs egress/bandwidth. we'll send a billing worksheet that shows per-token unit, embedding unit, and egress. for dedicated we can propose a reserved capacity price that bundles some egress, but large transfers remain a separate line item.
01:58 Ethan: from legal — the DPA has a couple exceptions we flagged: subprocessor notification lead time, audit rights in prod, and a specific clause on encryption-at-rest key control. can Redwood support BYOK with customer KMS?
02:12 Sofia: we do support BYOK on private deployments and Dedicated with KMS integration; on hosted api we have vendor-managed keys but can offer customer-managed keys in certain enterprise flows. the integration path differs and we need a KMS deep-dive.
02:34 Ethan: okay good, we will want to see key rotation, HSM details, and an ops runbook.
02:41 Jordan: we'll share our security pack and SOC2 artifact summary. note that FedRAMP was asked earlier — we don't have FedRAMP in this region, call it out as a blocker if that is non-negotiable.
03:02 Maya: right, not FedRAMP required for this line of business. next, SLA — we were hoping for 99.95 P99 but procurement understands ML infra has variability. can we do conditional acceptance?
03:18 Jordan: proposal: pilot window with 99.5% P99 for first 30 days, with credits for degradations and a rollback path to alternate model variants that are cheaper/have higher availability. post-pilot we revisit to 99.9 if benchmarks meet expectations. this is conditional SLA language we can draft.
03:36 Ethan: legal would like the credit remediation spelled out and also the measurement methodology (synthetic vs production).
03:44 Sofia: measurement we prefer synthetic steady-state runs we can both run; also tokenization and seq length impacts p99 heavily — include your expected average sequence length.
04:02 Priya: avg seq will be around 120 tokens for generation and roughly 40 for embeddings calls. our session windows can spike to 512 occasionally.
04:14 Sofia: that 512 spike drives kernel selection and memory pressure. we'll note that in the benchmark plan.
04:25 Liam: budget question again — is there a volume tier discount if we commit to reserved capacity for 6 months vs month-to-month?
04:33 Jordan: yes, reserved commits come with stepped discounts and lower per-token unit costs. we have example tiers in the worksheet.
04:41 Maya: on DPA exceptions — subprocessor lead time, we need 30 days notice for subprocessor changes. current language was 15 days. is that negotiable?
04:52 Jordan: standard is 15 but for enterprise we can extend to 30 with a DPA addendum. we'll flag that.
05:03 Ethan: also need clarity on audit logs retention and what level of PII gets redacted in logs.
05:10 Sofia: logs can be configured at route level; we provide structured tracing and token-level cost breakdown in console. PII redaction is possible but we'd need your examples.
05:26 Priya: we'll surface a couple of use cases that show what needs to be redacted.
05:32 Jordan: good. next — pilot scope. recommended: 2-week pilot with a single model variant, x qps ramp, and success metrics of p99 under the conditional threshold and error rate under 0.05%.
05:48 Priya: 2 weeks sounds ok, but need to know rollback actions if we break thresholds in production, e.g., route to smaller model or reduce batch sizes.
05:58 Sofia: we can configure smart routing and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants or cross-region fallback — that can be part of the runbook. note, cross-region may have data residency implications so we'd only use that if agreed.
06:18 Ethan: legal wants a clear clause: "conditional SLA during pilot with remediation credits and an explicit sign-off to increase SLA after successful pilot". can you draft that?
06:27 Jordan: yes. action item for us to draft conditional SLA wording.
06:33 Maya: timeline — procurement needs price and DPA exception responses by next Tuesday to keep the committee on track.
06:40 Jordan: understood — we'll prioritize.
06:45 [crosstalk — brief side conversation about stakeholder availability]
07:00 Sofia: technical notes — i'll ask for your sample payloads (Priya) in a standard ndjson so the bench is consistent. i'll also include p99, p50, median, and 95/99 tails in the results.
07:14 Priya: i'll share by end of day. also question about SSO: we need SAML/Okta integration. is that in GA?
07:23 Jordan: SSO via SAML and OIDC is GA, we also support SCIM for provisioning.
07:30 Liam: any hidden fees? like costs for on-prem connectors or private peering?
07:36 Jordan: private peering and dedicated interconnect are add-ons and will be listed; we can show an example TCO vs hosted.
07:45 Ethan: can you provide a redline-friendly DPA we can circulate? the version we have had a couple of redline points already.
07:52 Jordan: yes we'll attach a DPA variant and highlight suggested enterprise addendum language (30-day subprocessor notice, BYOK clauses).
08:00 Maya: ok great. last question — competitor diligence. we've done some calls with other providers and want to know differentiation points you think are relevant to procurement.
08:10 Jordan: we focus on serving economics and predictable SLOs across hosted/dedicated/private — that and a consistent API. also tooling: cost breakdown, rollouts, and fallback policies. we won't pretend to have check-box parity on every compliance cert but we'll be transparent about gaps.
08:26 Ethan: legal will review the DPA and the conditional SLA draft, procurement will await the pricing worksheet.
08:34 Jordan: recap: Jordan send pricing/egress worksheet and DPA addendum draft; Sofia run perf tests and share bench results; Stellar to share payloads, QPS targets, and DPA exception list.
08:50 Maya: agreed. thanks everyone.
08:54 Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the KMS deep-dive and the pilot start window.
09:00 [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: speaker turns sometimes merged; product names slightly mis-transcribed (Redwood Dedicated/Privet). timestamps are approximate.
